messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
Structure in this sentence is a complex rhetorical form combining an imperative command, a semicolon, and a long rhetorical question with dependent when clauses. Structure
Language in this passage uses archaic or Early Modern English spellings such as Consydre, thou, myne, hym, wyth, and penurye, creating a biblical or formal tone. Language
Meaning in this passage the speaker urges a listener to consider the speaker’s condition and father’s blindness, destitution, infirmity, and poverty, then refuses to abandon a helpless parent when the speaker has power to make the father’s remaining years comfortable and joyful. Meaning
